about.title: Rolling Hills Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Rolling Hills sees far fewer collisions than its denser Los Angeles County neighbors, but that doesn't make a crash here any less disruptive when it happens. The winding, gated roads around Crenshaw Boulevard, Crest Road West, Pathfinder Road, and the 900 Block of Silver Spur Road carry local and cut-through traffic alike, and public records show reported crashes tend to cluster on Monday late mornings into early afternoon. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the choices you make in the days after matter: photographs fade from memory, vehicle damage gets repaired, and insurance adjusters move quickly to lock in a story. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your situation and, if appropriate, take your case on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Deadline Is Closer Than It Seems
items.desc: You generally have two years from the accident to file a claim under California law, but if a government-maintained road was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to sort out fault or injuries can quietly cost you your right to file at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover a share of damages reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help make sure the insurer isn't unfairly inflating your share of blame.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Hurt You Later
items.desc: There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering under California law, but an early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to undercut that value. It's worth speaking with an attorney before agreeing to any statement or quick settlement offer.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near the Silver Spur Road and Crest Road West area — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention if you haven't already, and try to document the scene with photos if it's safe to do so. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company before speaking with an attorney. Reporting the crash and preserving evidence early can matter a lot, especially on roads with limited traffic camera coverage.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to LawProactive or the attorney I'm connected with?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront fee to have your situation reviewed.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Rolling Hills?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like the county, is involved because of road conditions, that deadline can be much shorter — sometimes six months. It's best to talk with an attorney as soon as possible so you don't lose that window.
